dedupe_keys.name: epic environmental policy integrated climate model

description: EPIC is a cropping systems model first built to estimate how erosion affects soil productivity, for the 1980 Soil and Water Resources Conservation Act analysis. It simulates about eighty crops with one crop growth model and crop-specific parameters, on a daily step for up to hundreds of years. It covers radiation interception, biomass and yield, root growth, water use, nutrient uptake, water quality, nitrogen and carbon cycling, climate change and carbon dioxide effects. It predicts how management changes soil, water, nutrient and pesticide movement, soil loss, water quality and yields, and can cost erosion for optimal management. Applications include erosion and wind erosion losses, nutrient and pesticide runoff and leaching, climate change and drought impacts on yields, and soil carbon sequestration. Its sister model APEX extends it to watersheds and farms. The team spans Texas A&M AgriLife Research, USDA ARS and USDA NRCS. Coverage is generic, for fields with homogeneous soils and management. Access: EPIC v.1102 executables and example files are downloadable; the page says release is restricted to people working with the modelling team, and the source code is on request. It is not for commercial use and is covered by the GNU General Public License. Caveats: a field-scale model whose older editors may not fit newer versions. For simulation it gives drought, erosion and climate impacts on crop yield and soil for agricultural hazard and adaptation studies. Related catalogue records include DSSAT, APSIM and the GGCMI outputs.
